Last updated November 14, 2026.

Ohio property tax is assessed by the county auditor, and owners can file a valuation complaint with the county Board of Revision.

What the official sources say

  • A valuation complaint for the current tax year is filed with the county auditor on or before March 31 of the ensuing tax year or the closing date of first-half collection, whichever is later. (ORC 5715.19(A)(1) (eff. Mar. 20, 2026); source)
  • For homestead reduction, 'sixty-five years of age or older' means a person who attained age 64 before Jan 1 of the application year; permanently and totally disabled defined by impairment on Jan 1 of application year or agency certification. (ORC 323.151(B), (D); source)
  • The ORC 319.302 partial exemption (non-business-credit rollback) as amended (latest legislation HB 186, 136th GA; version eff. Mar. 20, 2026) provides 10% for farming property and, for residential property, 7.5% for the first tax year the amendment applies, with cumulative 2.5-point reductions in each of the following two years and 0% thereafter. The older flat '2.5% rollback' for owner-occupied residential should NOT be stated as current. (ORC 319.302(B) (excerpt only; full text and applicability dates not seen); source)
  • CAUV 'land devoted exclusively to agricultural use' includes parcels under 10 acres with average yearly gross income of at least $2,500 over the three prior years (or anticipated), and commercial agricultural uses (eff. Mar. 20, 2026 version). (ORC 5713.30(A)(2); source)
  • County prosecuting attorney institutes foreclosure of the state's tax lien in the treasurer's name upon delivery of a delinquent land tax certificate or master list, in a court or the county board of revision (ORC 323.66); prosecuted like mortgage foreclosure; publication three consecutive weeks if by publication. (ORC 5721.18 (eff. Oct. 3, 2023); source)
  • Any person entitled to redeem delinquent land may do so before filing of the entry of confirmation of sale (or before expiry of the alternative redemption period under 323.78) by tendering taxes, assessments, penalties, interest, charges and costs to the county treasurer. (ORC 5721.25 (eff. Apr. 7, 2009); excerpt partial; source)
  • 'Tax certificate' under 5721.30 is a document (physical, book-entry or electronic) at the treasurer's discretion and is distinct from the delinquent land tax certificate under 5721.13; 'certificate parcel' means the delinquent land described in a tax certificate. (ORC 5721.30(A)-(B) (eff. Nov. 2, 2018); source)

What we could not confirm

  • Homestead income limits and the current rollback percentages.

Under ORC 5715.19, complaints are due by March 31 or the close of first-half collection, whichever is later, according to the statute text the research opened.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Ohio mortgage foreclosures go through the court of common pleas and end in a sheriff sale.

What the official sources say

  • When a mortgage is foreclosed, a sale of the property shall be ordered by the court of common pleas having jurisdiction; court may order sale in parcels or as a whole. (ORC 2323.07 (eff. Sept. 11, 2008); source)
  • Sheriff calls three disinterested freeholders to appraise land levied upon; for residential property they must return an estimate within 21 calendar days of the clerk's order of appraisal. (ORC 2329.17(A)-(B) (eff. Mar. 20, 2019); source)
  • Land may not be sold for less than two-thirds of appraised value (subject to 2329.51 and 2329.52). (ORC 2329.20 (eff. Sept. 28, 2016); source)
  • Notice of sheriff sale must be published once a week for at least three consecutive weeks before the sale (or start of online sale). (ORC 2329.26(A)(1)(a) (eff. Sept. 28, 2016); source)
  • Court examines the sale and, if proper, within 30 days of return of the writ journalizes satisfaction and orders title transferred to purchaser (confirmation). (ORC 2329.31(A) (eff. Sept. 29, 2017); source)
  • Debtor may redeem from a sale at any time before confirmation by depositing with the clerk the judgment amount, costs, and 8% per annum interest on purchase money; there is no post-confirmation redemption right. (ORC 2329.33 (eff. Sept. 28, 2016); source)

Ohio repealed its estate tax for deaths on or after January 1, 2013, according to the Department of Taxation.

What the official sources say

  • Probate court may release an estate from administration if assets are $35,000 or less, or $100,000 or less where the decedent left everything by will to a surviving spouse (and other listed conditions). (ORC 2113.03 (eff. Jan. 13, 2012) - excerpt shows (1) and (2)(a) only; full text beyond excerpt not seen; source)
  • An owner may designate TOD beneficiaries of real property by a transfer on death designation affidavit, verified before an authorized person, recorded with the county recorder before the owner's death; title vests in beneficiary at death; no consideration or delivery needed. (ORC 5302.22(B), (C)(1), (D), (E), (F); source)
  • Seller disclosure form is not required for a transfer by a fiduciary during estate administration or by an heir who inherited and did not occupy within the past year. (ORC 5302.30(B)(2)(g), (n); source)
  • No conveyance fee on transfers among heirs/devisees of a common decedent for no money consideration, or pursuant to ORC 2113.61. (ORC 319.54(G)(3)(n), (s); source)
  • Ohio estate tax was repealed for individuals with a date of death on or after January 1, 2013; a sunset provision was added by HB 110 (134th GA). (Ohio Dept of Taxation Estate FAQ; ORC 5731.02 (tax applies to deaths before Jan. 1, 2013); source)

An Ohio land contract lets a buyer pay over time while the seller keeps title until the contract is paid.

What the official sources say

content:

Cash Home Buyers in Ohio

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

An Ohio deed is recorded with the county recorder, and the conveyance fee can apply.

What the official sources say

  • A deed must be signed by the grantor and the signing acknowledged before a judge or clerk of a court of record, county auditor, county engineer, notary public, or mayor. (ORC 5301.01(A) (eff. Jan. 30, 2014); source)
  • Transfer on death designation affidavits are recorded by the county recorder in the same manner and for the same fee as deeds. (ORC 5302.22(E); source)
  • Deeds and instruments conveying land must be recorded with the county recorder where the premises lie; until recorded they are fraudulent as to a subsequent bona fide purchaser without knowledge. (ORC 5301.25(A); source)
  • Land installment contracts must be recorded within 20 days after signing by both parties and a copy delivered to the county auditor. (ORC 5313.02(C); source)
  • The mandatory county auditor real property transfer (conveyance) fee is $1 or 10 cents per $100 (or fraction) of value of real property transferred, whichever is greater, with listed exemptions (e.g., transfers to confirm/correct a deed, gifts between spouses or parent and child, pursuant to court order not resulting from a sale, no-consideration transfers, transfers to a revocable trust). (ORC 319.54(G)(3) (eff. Apr. 9, 2025); source)
  • The grantor (seller) pays the 319.54(G)(3) fee and any county real property transfer tax levied under ORC Chapter 322 at deed delivery, via statement of value filed with the county auditor. (ORC 319.202(D) (eff. Sept. 30, 2025); source)
  • A county may levy an additional (permissive) real property transfer tax not exceeding 30 cents per $100 of value; the tax is levied on and paid by the grantor to the county auditor before the deed is presented to the recorder. (ORC 322.02(A) (eff. Apr. 9, 2025); source)

  • No conveyance fee on transfers among heirs/devisees of a common decedent for no money consideration, or pursuant to ORC 2113.61. (ORC 319.54(G)(3)(n), (s); source)
  • Ohio estate tax was repealed for individuals with a date of death on or after January 1, 2013; a sunset provision was added by HB 110 (134th GA). (Ohio Dept of Taxation Estate FAQ; ORC 5731.02 (tax applies to deaths before Jan. 1, 2013); source)
